Subject: PO template + invoice cadence / discount eligibility for pilot

Hi Mina —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement here — a couple of quick items we need to lock for the pilot (Medivista legal asked me to get these on paper before we route the PO):

1) Required PO header fields: our finance org insists on PO number, BU code, GL account, and cost center present on the invoice for ERP matching. Can Redwood accept invoices that include GL and cost-center columns?

2) Invoice cadence: we prefer a single monthly invoice per PO, but our AP team runs payment cycles weekly for some entities. Can Redwood support a monthly cadence while still exposing an "invoice-run" attribute for our ERP?

3) Net terms / discount carveout: Medivista standard is net60, but we can do net30 for a 1% early-pay discount. We are asking whether any onboarding/commitment discount is contingent on invoice frequency (i.e., discount only applied if we accept monthly invoices).

I attached our current PO template (Medivista_PO_Template_v2.pdf) and a short GL mapping csv to show the fields. Please let me know the minimum header fields you require to ensure discounts apply and how Redwood will tag invoices for our ERP.

Elena

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear list and the attachments, very helpful. Quick answers and a few clarifying asks from our side: 

- Yes, Redwood can accept GL + cost-center fields in the invoice lines. We can map those to our billing metadata so they flow to your ERP. For implementation we'll need an exact column header mapping (your CSV is great; we'll ask engineering to validate).

- Invoice cadence: we can produce a single monthly invoice per PO and include a metadata field "invoice_run" (values: weekly|biweekly|monthly) so your ERP can tag the record. That will not prevent us from generating the supporting transaction lines for weekly AP runs if Medivista requests them, but the official invoice document will be monthly if that's your preference.

- Discounts: discount eligibility can be tied to invoice cadence but we prefer to make it explicit on the PO via a tag (e.g., "discount_slab:Q1-10pct"). If the PO lacks the tag we fall back to the contracted pricing. If you want the 1% early-pay for net30, we'll need the PO to include the payment-term field (Net30) and an acceptance clause in the purchase order.

Action items from Redwood:
1) We will produce a one-page "pre-billing checklist" listing the exact invoice header and line-level fields we need.
2) Engineering will validate the CSV field names against our ingestion pipeline and respond with a mapping matrix.
3) Finance (cc'd: Karthik) — can you confirm whether we can accept net60 as default but apply a 1% early-pay adjustment if Medivista elects net30? Also please confirm how to treat discount tags when PO fields are missing.

I'll follow up with the checklist and a proposed PO header mapping by EOD.

Best,

Karthik / Mina — looping finance and CS for quick guidance so we can give Elena a concrete answer. Summary of what we need to lock today:

• Required PO header fields (proposed minimum): PO Number, Billing Entity, Tax ID / VAT id, Billing Contact Email, Delivery Location, BU Code, GL Account, CostCenter, Invoice Contact, Payment Terms (NetXX), Discount tag (optional).

• Pricing / discount treatment (proposal): for the pilot we offer a 'pilot discount' of 8% applied to committed spend if Medivista: 1) issues a PO that includes the Discount tag, and 2) accepts monthly invoice as the official invoice cadence. If Medivista instead requests weekly invoice-run documents and does not include the Discount tag on the PO, we would revert to standard list pricing.

• Net terms: Redwood finance is OK to accept Net60 as default for Medivista, but to enable early-pay adjustments we need Net30 explicitly on the PO. For accounting we would apply the early-pay discount at cash-application time and reflect it as a line-level credit on the subsequent statement.

• Edge cases: if PO is missing GL or cost-center we can accept the invoice but it will delay ERP matching; in that case discount eligibility is subject to a manual review unless the PO includes the Discount tag.

Karthik — can you confirm acceptance of the above from a revenue recognition and collections perspective? If approved, Mina I recommend we send Elena the pre-billing checklist + a short "how to tag a PO for discounts" template (one paragraph) and offer a short call to walk Procurement through the fields.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior AM — Redwood Inference

Agree with Vanessa's proposal with one tweak: instead of making the full discount contingent on "monthly invoice as the official invoice cadence", let's require the Discount tag on the PO as the primary signal and treat invoice cadence as a secondary condition. That reduces rejected-discount tickets when AP runs internally on a different cadence. Operationally:

- Required: Discount tag present on PO (string field we can parse).
- Optional but preferred: invoice_run=monthly set on PO. If invoice_run is weekly and Discount tag is present, Finance will allow discount but we will require a confirmation email from Medivista AP acknowledging monthly consolidated invoicing for contractual pricing — we can accept weekly supporting runs for ERP if needed.

Also confirm revenue recognition note: if we apply early-pay credits they should be taken as an "other expense" line and will reduce AR once applied. No problem from RevRec as long as we document the policy.

Karthik
